ai_opportunities.title: Lead scoring + auto follow-up on every Justdial/Instagram/walk-in enquiry into Navrangpura and Surat batches
ai_opportunities.problem_solved: Enquiries arrive by phone, Instagram DM and walk-in at the Navrangpura centre and are handled manually with no evidenced CRM, so hot prospects (and now Surat prospects) go cold before counselling, and no one knows which source actually converts into paid seats.
ai_opportunities.applies_to: Enquiry-to-enrolment stage for the Navrangpura Ahmedabad batches (Justdial calls, Instagram DMs, walk-ins) and the new Surat launch enquiries
ai_opportunities.ai_mechanism: A lead-scoring model plus LLM enquiry summarisation. Inputs: raw enquiry records (caller number, Justdial listing source, WhatsApp/Instagram text, course asked about, budget/fee question, batch timing), historical enquiry-to-enrolment outcomes from Acedmicx student records, and fee/batch master. A gradient-boosted model (or Gemini API structured extraction first, gradient boosting once 300+ labelled outcomes exist) outputs: course interest, intent tier A/B/C, expected fee band, and recommended next action. An LLM step turns each raw call note or DM into a normalised record (course, city, timing, objection) and drafts a personalised WhatsApp message referencing the exact batch schedule and fee for that course. Workflow change: instead of a counsellor writing up leads after hours, every enquiry is scored within 5 minutes, A-tier leads are pushed to the counsellor's queue with a drafted reply and an Exotel/WhatsApp click-to-call, B/C tiers enter a 3-touch drip, and the counsellor only writes the closing message. Handoff to human at A-tier and at any fee-negotiation or B2B request.
ai_opportunities.expected_impact: Recovers a slice of leaked enquiries and lifts enquiry-to-enrolment conversion, worth roughly ₹8-18 L of incremental course revenue per year.

## 3. Potential Business Challenges

### ch-1 · Financial contraction and thin capital are constraining reinvestment and delivery capacity [7][1]
_Operational · severity high · confidence high_

Leadership is running batches, trainer payroll, portal maintenance and a Surat launch on declining cash and a very thin capital base. Day to day this shows up as delayed spending on curriculum, facilities, marketing or trainer hiring, and as founder/team bandwidth absorbing gaps instead of new investment.

**Reasoning:** S1.F10 shows FY25 revenue below ₹10 Cr, while S1.F11 reports a -54% 1-year revenue CAGR and S1.F19 a -71% 1-year EBITDA CAGR. S1.F6/S1.F7 show authorised and paid-up capital of only ₹1L each, S2.F2 says the company is unfunded, and S2.F3 gives a Tracxn Score of 22/100. The causal chain is: sharp revenue and EBITDA decline + minimal paid-up capital + no external funding → operating cash flow is fragile → every new trainer salary, Surat setup cost, marketing spend or platform upgrade must be self-funded → the company is likely to delay or underfund delivery-critical investments, which can further weaken enrollment and margins.

**Signals:** S1.F10: FY25 revenue less than ₹10 Cr; S1.F11: 1-year revenue CAGR -54%; S1.F19: 1-year EBITDA CAGR -71%; S1.F6 and S1.F7: authorised and paid-up share capital ₹1L each; S2.F2: no funding rounds raised; S2.F3: Tracxn Score 22/100

**Business impact:** The company is already contracting sharply: revenue CAGR -54% and EBITDA CAGR -71% in the last year. With revenue below ₹10 Cr and only ₹1L paid-up capital, even modest trainer hiring, Surat launch costs or batch-level operating losses can consume the buffer. The likely cost is slower growth, deferred reinvestment, and heightened risk that a weak quarter or delayed enrollment cycle hits cash and service quality.

### ch-2 · Trainer retention and hiring risk from low employee sentiment [12][5][3][10][4]
_Operational · severity high · confidence medium_

Trainers are the core delivery asset, but internal sentiment is poor and the company is actively hiring Technical Trainers while preparing for expansion. Day to day this can appear as trainer turnover, schedule gaps, inconsistent teaching quality and pressure on remaining faculty to cover extra batches.

**Reasoning:** AmbitionBox shows an overall 2.2/5 rating and work-life balance 2.4/5 from 9 employee reviews, which is a direct low-internal-sentiment signal even though Justdial customer ratings are high at 4.9/5 across 1,028 reviews. The profile also shows active hiring of experienced Technical Trainers via LinkedIn and a Surat expansion plan. The causal chain is: low employee ratings + active hiring for expansion → trainer supply is tight and retention is at risk → trainer turnover or unfilled roles create batch gaps and variable teaching quality → student experience and brand reputation can deteriorate despite strong historical customer reviews. Confidence is medium because the employee sample is small, but the direction is clear.

**Signals:** AmbitionBox: 2.2/5 overall from 9 employee reviews; AmbitionBox: work-life balance 2.4/5; Expansion plan: actively hiring experienced Technical Trainers via LinkedIn; Expansion plan: Surat expansion with advanced IT training; Justdial: 4.9/5 across 1,028 reviews, faculty praised as friendly and supportive

**Business impact:** Trainer replacement and ramp-up costs rise, and unfilled trainer roles can force batch cancellations or larger class sizes. The operational cost is slower batch delivery and lower student satisfaction; the commercial cost is weaker referrals and harder premium pricing.

### ch-3 · Surat expansion execution is under-resourced for a second-city launch [3][7][1]
_Operational · severity high · confidence medium_

The company has announced Surat expansion and is hiring trainers, but it remains a small, thinly capitalised Ahmedabad-based entity. **Reasoning:** The profile shows an announced Surat expansion with advanced IT training and future-ready programs, plus active hiring of Technical Trainers. **Signals:** Expansion plan: Surat, Gujarat expansion announced via Instagram; Expansion plan: actively hiring experienced Technical Trainers; S1.F10: FY25 revenue less than ₹10 Cr; S1.F6 and S1.F7: ₹1L authorised and paid-up capital; S2.F2: unfunded, no funding rounds; S1.F19: 1-year EBITDA CAGR -71%

**Business impact:** Launch costs in Surat can consume scarce cash before the new center reaches break-even. If the expansion is slower than planned, fixed trainer and facility costs hit margin while Ahmedabad receives less management attention. The business impact is lower profitability, potential brand inconsistency across cities, and a higher risk that expansion commitments are scaled back mid-launch.

Students choose IT training for career outcomes, but the profile shows an education-management portal for login and administration rather than a visible placement or outcome tracking system. The causal chain is: no evidenced outcome tracking → counselors and marketing cannot substantiate career ROI with data → high-intent students may choose competitors with placement statistics → referrals and B2B training contracts weaken over time.
